summary: Alfred Ludwig was an indologist and linguist who studied at the universities of Vienna and Berlin, learning under teachers including Albrecht Weber and Friedrich Müller. He held posts at the University of Vienna (1858) and Charles University (from 1860).

Alfred Radcliffe-Brown studied at the University of Cambridge and Trinity College. He held academic posts at the University of Sydney (~1925–1931), University of Chicago (~1931–1937), University of Oxford (~1937–1946), and Fundação Escola de Sociologia e Política de São Paulo (~1942–1944).

Ali S. Asani is a scholar of religious studies and indology who studied at Harvard College (~1973–1977) and Harvard University (~1977–1984). From circa 1984, he has served as a professor of Middle Eastern studies and religion at Harvard University.

Alice Harris is a linguist who studied at the University of Massachusetts Amherst and Harvard University (~1970–1976). She held academic posts at Vanderbilt University (~1979–2002) and the University of Massachusetts Amherst (~2009).
Alice Y. Tseng works in japanology and history/archaeology. She was a graduate student under Eugene Y. Wang (attested 2005) and served as a professor at Boston University (attested 2013).

Alicia Turner is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago (attested 2009), where her doctoral supervisors were Bruce Lincoln and Steven Collins, and studied under Saw Tun, Than Than Win, and others.

Alison Denton Jones works in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Martin King Whyte as well as teachers Allan H. Barr, Mingfei Gao, and Margaret H. Dornish.

Alka Patel is a scholar of history, archaeology, indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at Mount Holyoke College (BA ~1985–1989) and Harvard University (PhD ~1993–2000), becoming an associate professor at UC Irvine around 2007.

Allan G. Grapard was a scholar of japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at INALCO. He held posts as ISF Professor of Shinto Studies (~1985–2004) and Professor Emeritus at the University of California, Santa Barbara.

Allan Gibbard is a philosopher who earned his BA at Swarthmore College (~1959–1963) and PhD at Harvard University (~1965–1971). He held faculty posts at the University of Chicago (1969–1974), University of Pittsburgh (1974–1977), and University of Michigan (1977–2016).
Allan H. Barr is a sinologist who completed a doctorate at the University of Oxford in 1983. He served as Professor of Asian Languages and Literatures at Pomona College (attested 2001).

Allen Wright Thrasher is an indologist who studied under doctoral supervisor Daniel H. H. Ingalls and traditional teachers V. B. Deo, R. S. Raghavachariar, and K. A. S. Sastri. He worked at the Library of Congress (~1987–2011).
Allison Busch was an indologist who studied under Sheldon Pollock. She held an appointment as Associate Professor of Hindi Literature at Columbia University (attested 2026).
Alnis Dickson is an active scholar in Buddhist studies and tibetology who earned an MA at McGill University (attested 2009) under supervisor Lara Braitstein and teacher G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Alois Anton Führer was an indologist and archaeologist who earned his PhD at the University of Würzburg under Julius Jolly. He held posts at the State Museum Lucknow (1884–1899) and the Archaeological Survey of India (~1885–1898).
Alois Müller was a linguist who served at the Vienna University Library (~1860–1901), Palacký University Olomouc (1874–1879), and as director at Graz University Library (1879).

Aloysius Pieris is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies with degrees from London, Sri Lanka, and Tilburg. He founded and directed the Tulana Research Centre (1974) and held chairs at Washington Theological Union, Union Theological Seminary, and Vanderbilt.
Alubomulle Sumanasara is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from circa 1980 to 1986 under the guidance of professor Yasuaki Nara.

Alva Noë is a philosopher who studied at the University of Oxford (~1986–1988) and Harvard University (~1989–1995). He has held faculty posts at UC Santa Cruz (~1996–2003), City University of New York, and UC Berkeley (~2003).

Alvappillai Veluppillai was a scholar of indology, religious studies, and linguistics. Educated at Ceylon and Oxford under Thomas Burrow, he held posts at the University of Ceylon, University of Jaffna, Uppsala University (1990–2000), and Arizona State University (2002–2009).
